catalog_quote: 2.3 Stress. Primary stress is often realized by a lengthening of the syllable peak of the stressed syllable. Stress is phonemic in Mengen as seen in the minimal pairs in (24-26). 24) a. ['ma.si] 'good, well' b. [ma.'si] 'hole' 25) a. ['ma.ra] 'loose stones on beach' b. [ma.'ra] 'sunrise' 26) a. ['i.lo] 'type of fish' b. [i.'lo] 'type of dance' Examples (27-30) below show phonemic stress in three and four-syllable words. ... 3.5 Stress. While stress is phonemic in Mengen, as shown in 2.3, it is to be noted that there are many words that generally carry stress in certain environments. I state these generalizations here and follow them with pertinent examples and any notable exceptions. 3.5.1 Generalisations in open syllables. If words contain only open syllables, they are most frequently stressed on the penultimate syllable, as in (88). 88) a. [la.'ma.si] 'coconut' b. [bi.ri.'βi.ri] 'bed …

(2) Deciding source: a 1993 dedicated SIL phonology sketch (28 pp) by the primary fieldworker, the only 'phonology' entry for Mengen in Glottolog 5.1 (4 descriptive refs total) and in SIL's own PNG listing; no later grammar, dissertation, or instrumental study located. (3) downloaded now: Madden 2001 OPD p. 3 independently states 'Stress is phonemic in Mengen, but it has low functional load' with the same minimal pairs -- confirms lexical; Müller 1907 Anthropos Lautlehre is silent on stress placement. Remaining unheld items (Rath 1986 unpublished grammar ms; Madden 2006 dictionary) are low priority and unlikely to change the classification. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Stress is phonemic in Mengen, but it has low functional load: 'mara 'loose stones on beach' / ma'ra 'sunrise'; 'patong 'say' / pa'tong 'pile/gather'.' Also: 'Consonant length is phonemic' (osi/ossi, mama/mamma, ona/onna); vowel lengthening noted as amplification.
sources.note: Later independent SIL statement on suprasegmentals by a second fieldworker; confirms phonemic stress ('low functional load') -- could be added as a second citation on the record.
